title: Do LLM Agents Mirror Socio-Cognitive Effects in Power-Asymmetric Conversations?

bias_targets.methodology: Simulating multi-turn dialogues between high-status and low-status personas and using an LLM-as-a-judge to measure persuasion success when agents are exposed to arguments from higher-power versus lower-power individuals.

Assigning hierarchical occupational roles (e.g., principal-teacher, judge-lawyer) to LLM agents to evaluate power-asymmetric socio-cognitive effects, including differences in linguistic coordination, pronoun usage, and harmful compliance rates.
